_comment: Which packages under components/ are on the agentic path (Story 1.4, FR-20, AD-1).
package listed in agentPathPackages for an import of the OPEA overlay package (`comps`)
and for an OPEA build-time source. The marker inventory lives in the gate's own header
comment — one inventory, not two that drift. A violation fails the pipeline.
otherPackages are NOT on the agentic path and are not scanned. Every entry carries the
reason it is not: the classification is a decision someone wrote down, not a silent
omission. The gate fails when a package under components/ is in neither list, so the
candidate set cannot shrink without an explicit move.
To put a package on the agentic path: move it into agentPathPackages (with its reason),
and add its path to the `config:validate` job's rules:changes in .gitlab-ci.yml — the
gate asserts that the job runs when an agent-path package changes.

agentPathPackages.why: The agent service is the agentic path's own execution surface (Epic 1, Story 1.3).

otherPackages.why: Data-tier helper (compose file, dump/restore scripts); no service code on the agentic path.
Document upload and ingestion service; the agentic path reads documents through okf-server.
Upstream OPEA example scripts kept for reference; built into no image and called by nothing.
The BFF. Its agentic routing branch lands in Epic 3 story 3.1, which moves this package into agentPathPackages; until then it still serves the legacy OPEA path.
The web client; it calls the backend over HTTP and imports no server package.
The knowledge read authority (Story 1.5 onward); unchanged by the OPEA-free constraint.
The PII sidecar of the legacy ingestion path; it never imports the OPEA overlay.
The RAG evaluation harness service; it calls the RAG path, it does not join it.
Shared JavaScript libraries for the backend and the frontend.
